newsitem.title: MEXICO: Light selling nudges Mexican stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Light selling nudges Mexican stocks to lower close.

text.p: Mexican stocks slid Friday with buyers waiting for the Federal Reserve meeting next week, while light volume exaggerated the drop, traders said.
"Nothing's happening, people just aren't buying, and in low volume, the sales that are made move the IPC downwards quite a bit," said a trader from the Abaco brokerage.
The blue-chip IPC index closed 30.10 points down, or 0.90 percent, at 3,318.23. Volume was dull at 66.6 million shares traded.
Financial stocks were the main winners on Friday, due to selective and speculative buying, traders said.

Financial stock GFInver BCP series headed the gainers list, on rumors of a forthcoming alliance with the Spanish Santander bank, and gained 12.28 percent to 1.28 pesos. It was followed by GFBital B, L and A series shares.

"GFBital share prices are very cheap compared to book value. Also, their bank branches strategy is notably upping their market share, their reserves are good and dealers are buying ahead of what they see as a good third quarter report," said Daniel Romo, equity analyst at the Bancrecer brokerage.
Of 110 stocks traded, losers outnumbered winners by 61 to 28, with the remaining 21 unchanged.
